gap: No result ChatGPT got gives a price for any 1 kWh station that can run a 1,500 W heater. On 2026-11-14 the cheapest one with 1,800 W continuous is the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Classic at $459 on EcoFlow's US store (about 35 min on high). For $879 (EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max, 2,048 Wh, 2,400 W) or $899 (BLUETTI Elite 200 V2, 2,080 Wh, 2,600 W), heater time roughly doubles to about 70 min at about the same cost per heater-minute of $12.6–13.1.
standout_why: I compared against the four rivals ChatGPT cited. Tested Watts names no models and no prices. UTrendCo lists 11 models with runtimes but no prices. Lights On Lab lists 8 models with only 'check price' links. Volt & Valley prices one model, the EcoFlow DELTA 2 Max at $1,028.99, which is a 2 kWh unit. None of them prices a 1 kWh unit, compares the cost per heater-minute, or names the cheapest unit that clears 1,500 W with headroom. Our own current page has no prices either; its Jackery Explorer 1500 row says 'not read'.
decides: This confirms the page's answer that a 1 kWh unit gives about half an hour, and it adds a buying rule. If the heater has to run on high, the cheapest workable 1 kWh unit is $459 (DELTA 3 Classic). The BLUETTI AC180 at $499 gives the most minutes in the 1 kWh class (about 39 min). Spending about $420 more on a 2 kWh unit doubles the time at no extra cost per minute. Jackery's 1,500 W units (HomePower 1000 v2 at $549, and the Explorer 1000 v2, sold on Amazon only in solar bundles from $749) cost more than the DELTA 3 Classic and have no headroom over the heater's draw.

findings.label: Price, EcoFlow US store
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Classic Portable Power Station (1024Wh)
findings.note: Read from the store's product data. The listing says '1800W Powerful Output: 3600W surge'. Heater runtime at the rivals' 85% convention: 1,024 × 0.85 / 1,500 = 0.58 h, about 35 min, or $13.1 per heater-minute. This is the cheapest 1,800 W-class 1 kWh unit found today. Amazon has the same unit at $462 (ASIN B0FQVC4RF5).
